Thank you very much to the former Minister, or Cabinet Secretary, who was responsible for steering, very agilely, the Bill that is now an Act during the last Senedd, and I was very pleased to work together with you. And, yes, as you remind us, it was the first time for this Senedd to operate in that entirely inclusive, collaborative way and to pass that legislation unanimously. It is my intention to try and work in that same way with everyone in this Chamber.

You will know that we have committed to bring forward new legislation in the area of housing—a number of specific Bills—in order to give better protections to renters, and to look at exactly what kinds of measures are needed here in Wales as we move forward. And I do hope that we can work together, every one of us, in order to follow the same approach that we followed in the last Senedd. I look forward to having initial meetings with party spokespeople in order for us to explain how we intend to move forward with the legislation—not in this area, clearly, but in the area of housing more generally.

You are quite right, this legislation in Wales is very broad in its scope, and it aligns, of course, with the legislation that was passed in England, but it builds on that and brings different elements in—safety and who is accountable, but also, yes, the residents' voice. I think it is crucial that we acknowledge the residents' voice in all of this, and the importance of including them as we move forward. So, I do intend to announce shortly that we will establish a forum for leaseholders, and the issue of building safety will be something very important that that forum will be discussing. That builds on the work that was happening during the last Government.

I very much appreciate that I had the opportunity to hear directly from the Cladiators as a campaign group, who have been tirelessly campaigning and talking about the work that needs to happen at pace. This morning, I also had an opportunity to meet with representatives from the leaseholders of the Sand Wharf in Cardiff and Swansea Point in Swansea, and to hear directly from them about what the current experience means for leaseholders and the concern and the worry that it causes. And certainly, speaking with them and speaking with the committee as well—. As we move forward, I hope that the local government committee will help us to scrutinise the regulations to do exactly what you suggest, which is to make regulations that will lie under the legislation now to make sure that that is clear and that those regulations are suitable. So, there is that work. There is a lot of work to do under this Act; it's not just passing the Act—there is so much work that needs to happen underneath that, and we do have a timetable for that. But the very first thing that I did was to bring forward that consultation on regulations about the costs of remediation, because I was aware that that was something that was weighing very heavily on a great number of people.

In terms of the expert, specialist workforce that's needed, certainly that is something that we are giving due attention to. As you know, building control departments and planning departments have lost workers, have lost staff, over a long period of time now, and, certainly, we are paying attention to that and how we can bring that expertise back in. Of course, the idea is that there would be three authorities leading on this work, and I think by doing it in that way—and I was pleased to support that amendment to the Bill as well—in doing it in that way—. We aren't expecting all 22 local authorities to take on this burden individually. We're going to do it in a regional way, and I think that that will create the specialist workforce that we are going to need. Thank you.

Diolch yn fawr iawn i'r cyn-Weinidog, neu Ysgrifennydd Cabinet, a oedd yn gyfrifol am lywio, yn ddeheuig iawn, y Bil sydd bellach yn Ddeddf yn ystod y Senedd ddiwethaf, ac roeddwn i'n falch iawn o gydweithio efo chi. Ac, ie, fel dŷch chi'n ein hatgoffa ni, roedd o'r tro cyntaf i'r Senedd weithredu yn y ffordd hollol gynhwysol yna a phasio'r ddeddfwriaeth yn unfrydol. Mae hi yn fwriad gen i i geisio gweithio yn yr un ffordd efo pawb yn y Siambr yma.

Mi fyddwch chi'n gwybod ein bod ni wedi ymrwymo i ddod â deddfwriaeth newydd i mewn yn y maes tai—nifer o Filiau penodol—er mwyn rhoi gwell gwarchodaeth i rentwyr, ac i edrych yn union ar ba fath o fesurau sydd eu hangen arnom ni yng Nghymru wrth inni symud ymlaen. A dwi yn gobeithio y gallwn ni weithio efo'n gilydd, bawb ohonom ni, er mwyn efelychu'r dull a ddefnyddiwyd yn ystod y Senedd ddiwethaf. Dwi'n edrych ymlaen at gael cyfarfodydd cychwynnol efo'r llefaryddion er mwyn inni fod yn egluro sut dŷn ni'n bwriadu symud ymlaen efo deddfwriaeth—ddim yn y maes yma, yn amlwg, ond yn y maes tai yn fwy cyffredinol.

Dŷch chi'n hollol iawn, mae'r ddeddfwriaeth yma yng Nghymru yn eang ei sgôp, ac mae'n cyd-fynd, wrth gwrs, efo'r ddeddfwriaeth a basiwyd yn Lloegr, ond mae'n adeiladu ar hynny ac yn dod ag elfennau gwahanol i mewn—diogelwch a phwy sy'n atebol, ond hefyd, ie, llais y trigolion. Dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n hollbwysig inni gydnabod llais y trigolion yn hyn oll, a phwysigrwydd eu cynnwys nhw wrth inni symud ymlaen. Felly, dwi yn bwriadu cyhoeddi cyn bo hir y byddwn ni'n sefydlu fforwm ar gyfer llesddeiliaid, a bydd mater diogelwch adeiladu yn rhywbeth pwysig y bydd y fforwm yna yn ei drafod. Mae hwnna yn adeiladu ar y gwaith a oedd yn digwydd yn ystod cyfnod y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf.

Dwi'n gwerthfawrogi'n fawr iawn fy mod i wedi cael cyfle i glywed yn uniongyrchol gan y Cladiators fel grŵp ymgyrchu, sydd wedi bod yn ddiflino yn sôn am y gwaith sydd angen ei brysuro. Y bore yma, fe ges i gyfle hefyd i gyfarfod cynrychiolwyr o lesddeiliaid y Sand Wharf yng Nghaerdydd a Swansea Point yn Abertawe, a chlywed yn uniongyrchol ganddyn nhw beth mae'r profiad presennol yn ei olygu i lesddeiliaid a'r pryder y mae o'n ei achosi. Ac yn sicr, mae siarad efo nhw a siarad efo'r pwyllgor hefyd—. Wrth inni fynd yn ein blaenau, dwi'n gobeithio y bydd y pwyllgor llywodraeth leol yn helpu i graffu'r rheoliadau i wneud yn union beth dŷch chi'n awgrymu, sef i wneud y rheoliadau sydd yn mynd i orwedd o dan y ddeddfwriaeth rŵan i wneud yn siŵr bod hynna'n glir a bod y rheini'n bwrpasol. Felly, mae'r gwaith yna. Mae yna lot o waith i'w wneud o dan y Ddeddf, ddim jyst pasio'r Ddeddf—mae yna gymaint o waith sydd angen digwydd o dan hynny, ac mae gennym ni amserlen ar ei gyfer o. Ond y peth cyntaf un gwnes i wneud oedd dod â'r ymgynghoriad ynglŷn â rheoliadau ynglŷn â chostau cyweirio, achos roeddwn i'n ymwybodol bod hwnna'n pwyso yn fawr ar nifer fawr o bobl.

O ran y gweithlu arbenigol sydd ei angen, yn sicr, mae hwnna'n rhywbeth rydym ni'n rhoi sylw iddo fo. Fel rydych chi'n gwybod, mae adrannau rheolaeth adeiladu ac adrannau cynllunio wedi colli gweithwyr, wedi colli staff, dros gyfnod hir rŵan, ac, yn sicr, rydym ni'n rhoi sylw i hynny o ran sut medrwn ni ddod â'r arbenigedd penodol yna yn ôl. Wrth gwrs, y syniad ydy bod yna dri awdurdod yn arwain ar y gwaith yma, a dwi'n meddwl drwy wneud o fel yna—ac roeddwn i'n falch o gefnogi'r gwelliant yna ar gyfer y Bil hefyd—o'i wneud o mewn ffordd sydd wedi—. Dydyn ddim yn disgwyl i'r 22 awdurdod lleol gymryd y baich yma yn unigol. Rydym ni'n mynd i wneud o mewn ffordd ranbarthol, ac felly dwi'n meddwl bydd hwnna'n creu'r gweithlu arbenigol rydym ni'n mynd i fod ei angen. Diolch.

Can I thank you, Cabinet Minister, for your statement today? There are many sentiments within it that I align with, especially regarding the victims of Grenfell. Our hearts still go out to them and their families.

Every resident in Wales deserves to know their home is safe, that identified risks are being addressed swiftly, and that they will not be left facing years of uncertainty while Governments debate responsibility. Progress must be measured by outcomes. For too long, many people across Wales have faced uncertainty about the safety of their homes, the costs they may face and the timescales for remediation.

We must ensure that those responsible for building failures contribute towards putting them right. Residents who bought or rented homes in good faith should not be left carrying the burden of mistakes made by others. I note the announcement of the Wales interim measures alarm grant, which will provide support for leaseholders facing the costs of interim alarm systems. Now, while any assistance for affected residents will be welcome, leaseholders will want clarity on how many people are expected to benefit, how quickly support will be available, and whether the scheme will fully address the costs many residents continue to face as a consequence of failures for which they bear no responsibility.

Looking now at remediation orders, as well as the need to hold developers to account, the key test is not how many powers are available, but how quickly unsafe buildings are fixed and how many families are able to move on with their lives. There are concerns about the pace of progress. Clearly, we've heard them all today, and you acknowledge those yourself. But people need confidence that meaningful action is being taken now, and that remediation will not be delayed. As always in Wales, we need action, not more bureaucracy.

Minister, there is also a wider challenge here. You have made it clear that increasing housing supply is one of your priorities, with ambitions for 20,000 new social homes by 2030. Now, while increasing supply is important, quantity must never come at the expense of quality. And some of you may have heard Radio Wales this morning, where they were talking about snagging—so many new houses that have got so many faults. Well, we can't have poorly built houses in the first place, and the lessons of past building failures must be fully embedded in future development, so that every new home is built to the highest standard of safety, quality and resilience.

At the same time, Wales faces a housing crisis. We need more homes, but we need safe homes. We need faster development, but we also need public confidence that safety standards are being rigorously upheld. These objectives are not in conflict. They must go hand in hand. We also recognise that public confidence depends on ensuring that all significant safety risks are addressed, whether they relate to cladding, asbestos, reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete or wider structural concerns. People deserve safe homes, clear information and swift action when problems are identified. Therefore, can you, Minister, confirm how many leaseholders are expected to benefit from the Wales interim measures alarm grant? What assessment has been made of whether the scheme will meet the costs faced by affected residents? And what assurances can you provide that remediation work and developer compliance will accelerate well before the planned registration of the category 1 buildings, as you mentioned, in December 2027?

Ultimately, success will not be judged by the number of strategies, working groups or announcements; it will be judged by whether families can sleep safely in their homes and whether the public can have confidence that the failures of the past are not repeated. Diolch.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, Peter, for those questions. Of course, I agree entirely with you: we do have to see action. That is what is important here, and that is why I held that meeting with the developers last week, in order to emphasise that very clear message that we do expect to see progress, and progress at pace, for the benefit of the people living with this ongoing concern and anxiety, because they are constantly reminded of what happened at Grenfell. And I do think it is important—. Thank you for mentioning that. It is important that we remember why we are doing this work. It does all go back to that tragedy seven years ago now. So, that was my message to the developers. I am accountable to leaseholders. I am not accountable to the developers. It is the leaseholders who are at the forefront of my thoughts, and through you in the Senedd I am also accountable to them, and that is why I will bring progress reports to you in this place.

And that close monitoring is happening. My officials speak to the developers on an ongoing basis and are trying to help them remove some of the barriers that are in place. But, at the end of the day, they do have to take their responsibilities seriously, and I do hope to see progress by the end of the year. That is what was in the previous Government's contract. They expected to see the work started by all developers by the end of this year. We are a long way from that point, but that is the expectation I am placing on them, and, if that does not happen, as I have explained, I will then have to take further steps, and I will start to talk specifically about problems in this Chamber, because I am accountable to you in that regard. 

In terms of the grant, I am pleased that you have welcomed that. This can be put in place very quickly, and we can get it out of the door as soon as possible. This morning I was speaking to a representative from Swansea Point in Swansea and he mentioned that there are around 240 buildings that he represents, and that those developments could benefit specifically from the grant. In Sand Wharf, there are 100 units that could benefit from this. 

The criteria will be made available very soon so that people can scrutinise those, but certainly the grant won't pay for waking watch costs, because those have been significant. We are now moving to grants for the alarms, and I do very much hope that those alarms can be permanent. You can put in temporary alarms that can be adapted for when the work has been completed and retained. So, hopefully that explains a little more on that.

Your point on social housing and the clear desire of this Government to increase the supply of social housing is entirely appropriate. Of course, safety standards have to be maintained. We are talking about community housing and social housing that is high quality, low carbon and safe. That is crucially important. It's part of the ambition of this Government that people in Wales should be able to access a safe and affordable home for the long term.

Diolch yn fawr iawn, Peter, am y cwestiynau yna. Wrth gwrs, dwi’n cytuno'n llwyr efo chi: mae’n rhaid gweld gweithredu. Dyna sydd yn bwysig yn fan hyn, a dyna pam roeddwn i wedi cynnal y cyfarfod efo datblygwyr wythnos diwethaf, er mwyn pwyso’r neges glir yna ein bod ni yn disgwyl gweld cynnydd, a chynnydd ar gyflymder, er mwyn lles y bobl sydd yn byw efo pryder parhaus oherwydd eu bod nhw'n cael eu hatgoffa drwy'r amser am beth ddigwyddodd yn Grenfell. A dwi'n meddwl ei bod hi'n bwysig—. Diolch i chi am sôn am hynny. Mae'n bwysig inni gofio pam rydym ni yn gwneud y gwaith yma. Mae o'n deillio nôl i'r drasiedi yna saith mlynedd yn ôl, bellach. Felly, dyna oedd fy neges i'r datblygwyr. Dwi yn atebol i'r lesddeiliaid. Dwi ddim yn atebol i'r datblygwyr. Y lesddeiliaid sydd ar fy meddwl i, a drwoch chi yn y Senedd dwi'n atebol iddyn nhw hefyd, a dyna pam byddaf i'n dod ag adroddiadau cynnydd i chi yn fan hyn.

Ac mae'r monitro agos yna yn digwydd. Mae fy swyddogion i yn siarad efo'r datblygwyr yn barhaus ac yn ceisio eu helpu nhw i gael gwared ar rai o'r rhwystrau sydd yna. Ond, ar ddiwedd y dydd, mae’n rhaid iddyn nhw gymryd eu cyfrifoldeb o ddifri, a dwi yn gobeithio gweld cynnydd erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn. Dyna oedd yn y contract gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol. Roedden nhw'n disgwyl gweld y gwaith wedi’i ddechrau gan bob datblygwr erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn yma. Rydym ni'n bell o hynny, ond dyna'r disgwyliad dwi'n gosod arnyn nhw, ac, os nad ydy hynny'n digwydd, dwi wedi egluro byddaf i yn gorfod cymryd camau pellach, a byddaf i yn dechrau sôn yn benodol am broblemau yn y Siambr yma, achos dwi'n atebol i chi yn hynny o beth.

O ran y grant, dwi’n falch eich bod chi yn croesawu hwnna. Mae hwn yn medru cael ei weinyddu yn sydyn iawn, i'w gael o allan o’r drws cyn gynted â phosib. Y bore yma, roeddwn i'n siarad efo cynrychiolydd o Swansea Point yn Abertawe oedd yn sôn bod yna ryw 240 o adeiladau mae o'n eu cynrychioli ac y byddai'r datblygiadau yna yn gallu cael budd penodol allan o'r grant. Yn Sand Wharf, mae yna 100 o bobl—100 o unedau—a allai gael budd allan o hwn.

Y meini prawf, bydd y rheini ar gael yn fuan iawn i bobl gael craffu'r rheini, ond yn sicr fydd y grant ddim yn talu am gostau patrolio adeilad ar droed, sef y waking watch, achos mae hwnna wedi bod yn gost sylweddol. Rydyn ni'n symud rŵan at grantiau ar gyfer y larymau, a gobeithio bod y larymau yna yn gallu bod yn rhai parhaol. Mae modd rhoi larymau dros dro i mewn sydd efo'r gallu i gael eu haddasu ar gyfer pan fydd y gwaith wedi cael ei orffen. Felly, gobeithio bod hwnna'n esbonio ychydig bach mwy am hynny.

Mae eich pwynt chi ynglŷn â chartrefi cymdeithasol ac awydd clir y Llywodraeth yma i gynyddu'r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithas yn hollol, hollol briodol. Wrth gwrs, mae safonau diogelwch yn gorfod eu cynnal. Rydym ni'n sôn am gartrefi cymunedol, cartrefi cymdeithasol o ansawdd uchel, carbon isel ac yn saff. Felly, mae hynny'n holl, holl bwysig. Mae o'n rhan o uchelgais y Llywodraeth yma fod pobl yng Nghymru yn gallu cael cartref diogel a fforddiadwy ar gyfer y tymor hir.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Minister, for your statement today.

contributions.text_english: I appreciate the update and that this Government is taking this work seriously to better support impacted residents. For years now, residents have been afraid in their own homes and have felt that this issue has not been given the attention it deserves. Despite receiving assurances that their property was safe when they moved in, one resident in Cardiff has shared that they face a £3,000 cost for a waking watch, which costs £15,000 a week between 96 flats, and the management company are having to find £150,000 to install fire-detecting equipment. Without the necessary improvements, residents have faced the possibility of being made homeless as their homes aren't safe to live in. I welcome the Minister introducing financial support as an interim measure while remediation works are carried out. How will the Minister make sure tenants don't have to pay out of pocket for remediation work again? Diolch.

contributions.text_english: Cabinet Minister, the building safety programme risks becoming yet another example of taxpayers being asked to foot the bill for failures that they did not cause. England regulates buildings above 18m under its strictest duties. Wales has brought every multi-occupied residential building of any height into the new framework. That's over 51,000 buildings, mostly owned by small private landlords. The Senedd's own committee called the compliance timeline 'unrealistic'. Has the Minister modelled the impact on housing supply and on the capacity of authorities that must enforce it, while residents living in the most dangerous buildings still wait? With housing affordability worsening and house building targets already being missed, can you provide evidence that these measures will not further slow housing delivery? Thank you.

There is a good pipeline of projects in place in that system. So, I don't really see a link between the two things. Thank you.
contributions.text_original: O ran y pwynt bod cysylltiad rhwng y gwaith yma a'r gwaith cyflenwi tai cymdeithasol, dwi ddim rili yn gweld bod yna gysylltiad. Mae'n rhaid i'r gwaith yma ddigwydd. Mae'n rhaid i'r adeiladau yma gael eu gwneud yn saff. Mae'r Ddeddf yn dweud hynny. Mae'r gwaith o gynyddu’r cyflenwad o dai cymdeithasol yn rhywbeth sydd yn mynd i ddigwydd yn raddol dros gyfnod. Mae yna pipeline da o brosiectau o fewn y system yna. Felly, dwi ddim wir yn gweld cysylltiad rhwng y ddau beth. Diolch.

contributions.text_english: And finally, Minister, Mike Hedges.
contributions.text_original: Ac yn olaf, Weinidog, Mike Hedges.

contributions.text_english: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. I welcome the update on the building safety programme and the steps the Government is taking to protect leaseholders and ensure that the homes covered by the programme are safe, and those living in them are treated with the fairness and dignity they deserve. This has been a long time coming. My constituents have waited a very long time for this to be resolved. It's created hardship and worry for my constituents. The commitment to provide financial support to leaseholders facing the cost of interim alarm systems required to support the simultaneous evacuation policy is a positive step, but it's an acknowledgement that, despite all the agreements, we have not reached the stage where work is going to be done everywhere in the near future. My constituents living in fear of being another Grenfell want the obligations under the contract to be met, and the Welsh Government needs to get legally enforceable agreements with guaranteed completion dates so that my constituents can sleep safely at night.
contributions.text_original: Thank you, Deputy Presiding Officer. I welcome the update on the building safety programme and the steps the Government is taking to protect leaseholders and ensure that the homes covered by the programme are safe, and those living in them are treated with the fairness and dignity they deserve. This has been a long time coming. My constituents have waited a very long time for this to be resolved. It's created hardship and worry for my constituents. The commitment to provide financial support to leaseholders facing the cost of interim alarm systems required to support the simultaneous evacuation policy is a positive step, but it's an acknowledgement that, despite all the agreements, we have not reached the stage where work is going to be done everywhere in the near future. My constituents living in fear of being another Grenfell want the obligations under the contract to be met, and the Welsh Government needs to get legally enforceable agreements with guaranteed completion dates so that my constituents can sleep safely at night.

contributions.text_english:
Thank you very much, Mike. You are also emphasising the hardship that some of your constituents have faced and are facing because of this situation, and the need to treat them with dignity, respect and fairness. Certainly, I am doing that. I met with a constituent from Swansea today who spoke about the concern that they have because of the slow progress with the development at Swansea Point in particular.

I understand your point in terms of providing grants for the interim alarms, and that that perhaps is a sign that things are going to slow down. However, what I know can happen is that these alarms can be installed as a temporary measure, but there is a way of adapting them so that they can remain there permanently. So, that is a sign that things can move forward, because those alarms can remain there after the work is completed.

Just to remind you, in closing, Dirprwy Lywydd, the requirement of the previous Government in the agreement with developers was that work was to be started in every building by the end of this year. That was the expectation. Perhaps that expectation hasn't been made clear enough to developers—I think it probably was—by the previous Government, but this Government is determined that the developers will take their work completely and entirely seriously.

I look forward to returning here to the Senedd, not to talk to you about the problems, but to tell a positive story about what's happened in Wales with the building safety programme. Thank you.
contributions.text_original:
Diolch yn fawr iawn, Mike. Rydych chi hefyd yn pwysleisio'r caledi y mae rhai o'ch etholwyr chi wedi bod ac yn wynebu oherwydd y sefyllfa yma, a'r angen i'w trin nhw efo tegwch a pharch ac urddas. Yn sicr, dwi yn gwneud hynny. Fe wnes i gyfarfod etholwr o Abertawe heddiw a oedd yn sôn am y pryder sydd ganddyn nhw oherwydd yr arafwch efo datblygiad Swansea Point yn benodol.

Dwi'n deall eich pwynt chi o ran rhoi grantiau tuag at larymau interim, a bod hynny efallai yn arwydd bod pethau mynd i arafu. Ond, beth dwi'n gwybod all ddigwydd ydy bod y larymau yma yn medru cael eu gosod fel mesur dros dro, ond mae yna ffordd o'u haddasu nhw fel eu bod nhw yna yn barhaol. Felly, mae hwnna yn arwydd bod pethau'n gallu symud ymlaen, oherwydd fe fydd y larymau yna yn gallu bod yna ar ôl i'r gwaith gael ei gwblhau.

Jest i'ch atgoffa chi, wrth i ni gloi, Ddirprwy Lywydd, gofyniad y Llywodraeth ddiwethaf yn y cytundeb efo'r datblygwyr oedd bod gwaith i ddechrau ym mhob adeilad erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn yma. Dyna'r disgwyliad. Efallai nad ydy'r disgwyliad yna wedi cael ei wneud y ddigon clir i ddatblygwyr—dwi'n credu efallai ei fod o—gan y cyn-Lywodraeth, ond mae'r Llywodraeth yma yn benderfynol bod y datblygwyr yn cymryd eu gwaith yn gwbl, gwbl o ddifrif.

Dwi'n edrych ymlaen at ddod yn ôl yma i'r Senedd, nid i sôn am y problemau, ond i sôn am y stori dda sydd wedi digwydd yng Nghymru efo'r rhaglen diogelwch adeiladau. Diolch.

contributions.text_english: Thank you very much, Cabinet Minister. That brings today's proceedings to a close. See you tomorrow.
contributions.text_original: Diolch yn fawr iawn i chi, Weinidog Cabinet. Daw hynny â thrafodion heddiw i ben. Fe wnaf eich gweld chi yfory.
